npc.old_smuggler.flavor_text: Cracked a door like that once. Cost me a hand and a good ship. You bring something worth the risk, we talk.
npc.wolf_barkeep.flavor_text: The lights are low and the patrons don't ask questions. A scratched sign above the bar reads NO MILITIA. The operator sizes you up.
step.bar_q1_oldhand.completion_flavor: Word has gone to Barnard's Star. The old man is deciding whether you want an answer or merely a door to break. Give him time.
step.bar_q1_oldhand.description: The Barkeep names an old smuggler who once found a door made of the same impossible material. It cost him a hand and left him with a story no one believes. Since the Incident, the Militia has been watching the old routes for anyone who asks the wrong questions.
step.bar_q1_oldhand.dialogue.barkeep.int: The old hand did not crack that door. He made it answer, and it took his hand for the courtesy. He is retired on Barnard's Star b now, living where the maps get vague. He owes the bar a favor, so I will send word. Keep your head down: since the Incident, the Militia has treated old routes like crime scenes.
step.bar_q1_oldhand.ready_message: The old man will see you for the right price. Come through the bar first; I have a crate that proves you can carry a secret without opening it in public. Run it to Barnard's Star b.
step.bar_q1_oldhand.title: The Old Hand
step.bar_q2_proof.completion_flavor: The old man is surveying the dig site with one hand and three decades of regret. Give him time to decide what part of the old story you are ready to carry.
step.bar_q2_proof.description: The old smuggler does not deal in introductions; he deals in proof. Take the Barkeep's hot crate to Barnard's Star b. Every Militia patrol on the route can scan it, and every one of them has a reason to wonder why you are carrying it.
step.bar_q2_proof.dialogue.barkeep.activ: The crate's in your hold. Get it to the old man on Barnard's Star b before a patrol sniffs it.
step.bar_q2_proof.dialogue.barkeep.intro: The old man will not deal with strangers, but he still owes the bar. I have one crate left: black-market weapons, hot enough to make a patrol curious. Deliver it to Barnard's Star b and he will draw the cave on your map.
The crate made it. Then listen carefully. The cave is up the ridge, and the power cell is still below. The old job was not a robbery; it was an attempt to make the door recognize a human signal. Fetch the cell. I will tell you the rest if you come back.
You brought the cell out. Good. It is old Militia hardware, which means someone still has a file on it even if the file says it never existed. Keep it away from scanners.
The bar sent word. You got the crate, or are we wasting both our times?
step.bar_q2_proof.ready_message: He has marked the cave where the old job went wrong. The rig's power cell is still below, along with whatever the old door did not take. Meet him at the dig on Barnard's Star b.
step.bar_q2_proof.title: The Proof Run
step.bar_q3_rigparts.completion_flavor: The power cell is decades old, unstable, and still holding a charge that does not decay like human power cells do. Take it to the only black-market rig built to handle it at the Wolf 359 listening post.
step.bar_q3_rigparts.description: The old smuggler drew the cave where the old job went wrong. Descend into the Barnard's Star b surface caves and recover the rig's power cell - decades-old militia-issue hardware.
step.bar_q3_rigparts.dialogue.old_smuggl: The cave's up the ridge, past the old dig markers. The cell is down in the dark - watch your step, and watch the sky. The militia's been circling.
step.bar_q3_rigparts.title: The Power Cell
step.bar_q4_blackmarket.completion_flavo: The operator connects the cell and immediately disconnects it again. The meter has no scale for what it reads. 'It has been waiting in the dark since before the Incident,' he says. 'Give me time. And do not let anyone ask why it still remembers the door.'
step.bar_q4_blackmarket.description: The power cell is in your hold - unstable and hot. Take it to the Wolf 359 listening post. The black-market operator there has the only rig that can recharge it.
step.bar_q4_blackmarket.dialogue.old_smu: A patrol took the cell? It was never going to travel quietly. I kept one spare casing from the old job. I can replace it once; after that, the route has to stay yours. Get it to Wolf 359.
step.bar_q4_blackmarket.dialogue.wolf_ba: The cell is on the rig. It is drawing power in pulses, like it is listening for a response. Give me time. I will send word when it is safe to move.
The cell is ready. I have warned the Earth Barkeep, and I have not warned the Militia. That is the difference between a delivery and a mistake. Watch the patrols.
You brought something that still has a Militia serial. Old model, clean enough to be dangerous. I can recharge it, but I am not going to tell you what the meter says when the numbers stop behaving.
step.bar_q4_blackmarket.ready_message: The cell is charged, though the operator refuses to say what charged it. Collect it at the Wolf 359 bar and keep it hidden on the return run. Every Militia scanner between here and Earth will notice the moment you enter Sol.
step.bar_q4_blackmarket.title: Black-Market Recharge
step.bar_q5_charged.completion_flavor: The cell is back on Earth. The rig can be assembled now.
step.bar_q5_charged.description: The charged cell is in the Wolf 359 bar. Collect it and run it back to the Barkeep on Earth. The Militia scanners in Sol will not merely see a hot crate; they will recognize an old signature and start asking why it has returned.
step.bar_q5_charged.dialogue.barkeep.act: The cell is here. Hand it over and let us see whether the old rig still knows what it was built to do.
step.bar_q5_charged.dialogue.barkeep.int: You made it back. Give me the cell before the scanners remember you. The rig is waiting, and I would like to finish one job in my life before the past catches up.
step.bar_q5_charged.dialogue.wolf_barkee: The cell is in your hold. Run it to Earth before the Militia decides the old signature is evidence enough to take you apart.
There it is. Fully charged, still carrying a signature the Militia thought it had erased. Take it to Earth. The moment you enter Sol, every patrol will have a reason to look twice.
step.bar_q5_charged.title: The Return Run
step.bar_q6_rig.description: Return to the Barkeep on Earth. The rig is assembled, but the old hand never promised it would open the door gently.
step.bar_q6_rig.dialogue.barkeep.intro: There she is - the old rig rebuilt for a door that was never meant to open. It does not crack the seal so much as convince the power feed to stop pretending it is dead. The Militia will watch you from here on. Welcome to the family, friend.
step.bar_q6_rig.title: The Rig
